# gitmoap_group_ai_org_squad_memory (Data Source)

A squad's memory page — what its agents share — at its newest revision or an earlier one. Read by the board, or by anyone who can read every repository the squad owns; a squad that owns none is the board's alone, and anyone else is answered not found. `revision` names an earlier revision while it is still kept.

The token needs `ai_org:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The organization's top-level group
- `squad_key` (String) The squad's key

### Optional

- `revision` (Number) An earlier revision still kept; the newest when omitted

### Read-Only

- `agent_handle` (String) The agent's handle, for an agent's page.
- `body` (String) The page, in Markdown; empty for a page nobody has written.
- `history` (Attributes List) The page's kept versions, newest first — each one readable with `?revision=`. Older ones
are no longer kept. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--history))
- `kind` (String) Which page: an agent's own, a squad's, or the organization's conventions.
- `note` (String) What the writer said changed.
- `updated_at` (String) When this version was written.
- `updated_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--updated_by))

<a id="nestedatt--history"></a>
### Nested Schema for `history`

Read-Only:

- `history_updated_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--history--history_updated_by))
- `note` (String) What the writer said changed.
- `revision` (Number) Its version number.
- `updated_at` (String) When it was written.

<a id="nestedatt--history--history_updated_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `history.history_updated_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
